s02.note: t=0 locate: the fit agrees with the tracker to 0.4 mm and the rod is lying on the board. t=1.56-6.24 grasp: top-down pinch at contact height. In k04 (t=6.24) the wrist view shows the orange rod clamped vertically between the fingertips and lifted. The policy's own fit puts the rod centre at z=6.8 mm in the TCP frame, which by plan.md's scale is at the tips, not in the pads. The grip is near one end: the rod centre sits 4.6 mm along the rod from the TCP, ext only 22 mm visible. Insert: the arm runs a 144-degree rotation chain (12 move_to_joints calls, t=10.76-18.92) to the fixture. In k05 (t=10.76) the rod is still between the fingers, tilted, above the blue fixture. In k06 (t=11.20) it is already separating, and in k07 (t=11.72) and k10 (t=13.04) the wrist view shows empty fingers with the rod lying on the board beside the blue fixture. The tip grip let go during the rotation, not because of any contact. The rest of the chain finished with an empty hand (tcp [0.341,0.070,0.082] at t=18.92). align 0 printed 'rod not seen in hand' and insert FAILed at t=19.12. After that the robot did nothing until the timeout. final.png: the rod lies on the board next to the fixture, the hand is empty. The tracker's part estimate stays frozen at the start pose for the whole trace, so it is useless here.

s03.note: t=0 locate: the rod lies close to the goal fixture, among clutter (fit centre [0.354,0.042]). Grasp: every first candidate collided with obstacles, so the policy pushed the rod along [0.32,-0.95] to [0.363,0.018] (t=2-8.3). Attempt 0 (t=9.2-14.7) closed, but the 4 mm-up check found the rod not held. Attempt 1, 2.5 mm higher (t=15.0-20.4), lifted it. In k08 t=20.40 the wrist view shows the rod vertical in the fingertips, and the global view shows it lifted above the board. The fit puts it 9.6 mm off-centre along the rod, at TCP-frame z 8.4 mm (tips). Insert: the first five yaw candidates were 'chain step 2 unreachable'. The chosen psi=-15 had 2976 hand-hit points and needed a 168-degree rotation. The rotation chain ran from t=25.6 to t=37.3. Every move_to_joints returned FAIL with err slowly shrinking from 0.15 to 0.014 while the tcp stayed near z 0.165: the joints were slewing slowly, not blocked, and the wrench stayed under 3 N. In the sheet frames at t=32-40 and in k21/k22 the wrist view shows the rod still held, near vertical, over the grey fixture region. The global view is blocked by the arm. align 0 measured a 13.7-degree tilt and 12 mm xy error; align 1 measured a 1.35-degree tilt, (-0.75,-1.35) mm xy error and z err -7.6 mm. At t=38.36 the arm moved to the pre pose (tcp z 0.09, ok). The episode timed out at 40 s, before any step-down, release or verifier. Almost all the time went to the push plus two grasp attempts (20 s) and the slow 168-degree rotation (12 s). final.png: the rod is still in the fingers above the fixture, not inserted.

Reaching that point took the only reachable candidate (2976 hand-hit pts, 168 deg) and 12 slow joint moves (t=25.6-37.3). The tcp did not stall on contact; the err fell steadily and the wrench stayed small. In final.png the rod is in the hand above the fixture, not in the bore.

s04.note: t=0 locate OK. t=1.64-7.80 grasp: pinch at contact height. The rod is lifted, vertical, between the fingertips (sheet t=8.0); the fit puts it at TCP-frame z 7.0 mm (tips), 4.5 mm off-centre along the rod, ext 24 mm visible. Insert: a 127-degree rotation chain (t=13.0-20.68) brings the rod over the fixture. In k15 t=20.68 the rod is still in the fingers but visibly tilted in the global view. The alignment loop then brought it to a 0.1-degree tilt and about 0.4 mm xy error over the bore, with the bottom at z 0.052 (pre pose). Four step-downs took the bottom to an estimated 0.0308, about 7 mm below the fixture top at 0.0376, with almost no force (|F| ~2-3 N, 'tcp short' ~0 mm). The policy then released. In the sheet frame at t=26.6 the rod is still vertical over the fixture. In k16 t=29.64 (after release) it leans about 27 degrees, its lower end at the fixture mouth: the policy's fit gives axis z 0.888, top 17 mm high, 12.8 mm off-axis. By the sheet frames at t=34-40 and final.png it has fallen over and lies flat on the board beside the fixture. A rod 7 mm deep in a close-fitting bore could not lean 27 degrees, so the bottom was very likely not inside the bore. Plausible cause: the bottom rested on the rim while the rod slid up in the tip grip, which would explain the free-looking descent; the release then let it topple. The hand only lifted after release and did not touch the rod again. Insert FAILed at t=29.64 for a correctly stated reason; the robot then idled until the timeout.

grasp.evidence: Rod lifted and vertical in the fingertips (sheet t=8.0, k04 t=7.80); fitted centre z 0.081. It was still held through the rotation and alignment (k15 t=20.68, sheet t=26.6). Weak: tip grip (TCP-frame z 7 mm), off-centre, and the rod hangs tilted after rotation (k15).

insert.evidence: Aligned over the bore (tilt 0.1 deg, xy 0.4 mm) and stepped down with no resistance to a claimed bottom of 0.0308, then released. Right after release (k16 t=29.64) the rod leaned about 27 deg at the fixture mouth: fit axis z 0.888, top +17.2 mm, 12.8 mm off-axis. It then fell flat onto the board beside the fixture (sheet t=34-40, final.png). It was never seated. The bottom most likely sat on the rim rather than in the bore (rod probably slipping in the tip grip during the 'free' descent), and nothing but its own toppling moved it after release.
